en: to make a slip of the tongue

examples.ko: 회의에서 제가 실언해서 정말 죄송해요.
examples.en: I'm really sorry that I said the wrong thing in the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 실언할까 봐 인터뷰를 거절했대요.
examples.en: They say he turned down the interview for fear of saying something wrong.

examples.ko: 긴장해서 발표 중에 실언한 것 같아 마음에 걸려요.
examples.en: I was nervous and think I misspoke during the presentation, and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 높은 사람일수록 실언하지 않도록 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The higher someone's position, the more careful they must be not to misspeak.

examples.ko: 실언했다고 인정하고 바로 사과하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to admit you misspoke and apologize right away.

examples.ko: 제가 방금 실언했어요, 잊어 주세요.
examples.en: I just said the wrong thing; please forget it.

explain: '말실수를 하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 친구 사이에서는 보통 '말실수'라고 하고, '실언'은 정치인이나 유명인의 말이 문제가 될 때 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. '실언을 하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The minister made a slip of the tongue in an interview and apologized.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실언하다'를 풀어 쓴 말로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out form of 실언하다 that is common in the news.
phrases.en_equiv: to make a slip of the tongue

phrases.en: I was nervous and said the wrong thing to my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '실언'보다 이 말을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life this is used far more than 실언.

phrases.en: I'm careful not to say anything inappropriate when I give a presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실수로 나쁜 말을 하지 않게 주의한다는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected phrase meaning to take care not to say something wrong by accident.
phrases.en_equiv: to be careful not to misspeak

explain_en: A verbal blunder in speech, somewhat formal (회의에서 실언하다) It means almost the same as '말실수를 하다' (to slip up in speech). Among friends people usually say '말실수', while '실언' often appears in the news when a politician's or celebrity's words cause trouble. You can also say '실언을 하다'.

en: to show no promise; to be hopeless

examples.ko: 어른에게 그렇게 말하다니 정말 싹수없어요.
examples.en: It's really rude to speak to an adult like that.

examples.ko: 싹수없는 행동을 하면 친구가 없어져요.
examples.en: If you behave rudely, you'll lose your friends.

examples.ko: 저 애는 인사도 안 하고 싹수없게 굴어요.
examples.en: That kid doesn't even greet people and acts disrespectfully.

examples.ko: 후배가 너무 싹수없어서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: My junior was so rude that I got angry.

examples.ko: 싹수없다는 말을 들으면 기분이 나쁘죠.
examples.en: It feels bad to be told you're disrespectful.

examples.ko: 싹수없던 동생이 요즘은 많이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: My rude younger sibling has changed a lot lately.

explain: 주로 버릇없고 예의가 없는 사람이나 행동을 나쁘게 말할 때 써요. 윗사람이 아랫사람을 평하거나 뒤에서 흉볼 때 들려서, 직접 면전에서 쓰면 아주 거칠어요. 반대로 잘될 가능성이 보이면 '싹수가 있다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저렇게 인사도 안 하면 싹수가 노랗다는 소리를 들어요.
phrases.en: If you never greet people like that, you'll be told you have no future.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘될 가능성이 전혀 안 보인다고 나쁘게 평가하는 말이에요. 주로 사람의 태도가 형편없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A harsh judgment that someone shows no sign of ever amounting to anything, usually because of a terrible attitude.
phrases.en_equiv: have no future; be a lost cause

explain_en: It is mainly used to criticize a person or behavior as ill-mannered and disrespectful. Because it is typically a senior judging a junior or gossip behind someone's back, saying it to someone's face is very harsh. The opposite is '싹수가 있다', meaning someone shows promise.

t90.ax: My junior was so rude that I got angry.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 오래된 앙숙이에요.
examples.en: The two of them are longtime enemies.

examples.ko: 우리 형과 동생은 만나면 앙숙처럼 싸워요.
examples.en: My older brother and younger sibling fight like sworn enemies whenever they meet.

examples.ko: 그 두 회사는 서로 앙숙 관계예요.
examples.en: Those two companies are rivals who hate each other.

examples.ko: 고양이와 개는 흔히 앙숙이라고 해요.
examples.en: Cats and dogs are commonly said to be sworn enemies.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 앙숙이던 친구와 지금은 제일 친해요.
examples.en: I'm now closest with the friend who was my enemy when we were little.

examples.ko: 앙숙 사이였던 두 나라가 드디어 화해했어요.
examples.en: The two countries that had been bitter enemies finally made peace.

explain: 서로 사이가 아주 나쁜 사람이나 집단에 써요. '원수'보다 무겁지 않아서 장난스럽게도 말할 수 있어요. 보통 '앙숙이다', '앙숙 관계'로 써요.

phrases.en: The two companies have long been bitter rivals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 집단 사이가 나쁜 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a bad relationship between people or groups.

phrases.example: 작은 오해 때문에 둘은 앙숙이 됐어요.
phrases.en: A small misunderstanding made the two of them enemies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 나빠지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the change into a bad relationship.

phrases.example: 그 둘은 학교 때부터 앙숙으로 지내요.
phrases.en: Those two have been at odds since school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 사이가 나쁜 채로 지내는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows staying on bad terms for a long time.

explain_en: It is used for people or groups that get along very badly. It is lighter than '원수' (enemy), so it can also be said playfully. It usually appears as '앙숙이다' or '앙숙 관계'.

en: to be narrow-minded; to be intolerant; to be petty

examples.ko: 그렇게 사소한 일로 화내는 건 옹졸해요.
examples.en: Getting angry over such a trivial thing is petty.

examples.ko: 저는 마음이 옹졸한 사람이 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to become a narrow-minded person.

examples.ko: 친구가 잘돼서 질투하다니 제가 너무 옹졸했어요.
examples.en: I was so petty to be jealous of my friend's success.

examples.ko: 옹졸하게 굴지 말고 한 번만 봐줘요.
examples.en: Don't be petty, just let it go this once.

examples.ko: 그 상사는 옹졸해서 작은 실수도 잊지 않아요.
examples.en: That boss is petty and never forgets even small mistakes.

examples.ko: 옹졸한 생각을 버리고 넓게 보세요.
examples.en: Drop the narrow thinking and look at the big picture.

explain: '속이 좁다'와 비슷한데, '옹졸하다'가 조금 더 딱딱한 말이에요. 사람의 마음이나 태도에 써요. 반대말은 '너그럽다', '대범하다'예요.

phrases.example: 작은 일에 화내는 옹졸한 사람이 되기 싫어요.
phrases.en: I don't want to be a petty person who gets angry over small things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 형태로, 마음이 좁은 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used for someone narrow-minded.

phrases.en: Don't be so petty toward your friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '굴다'와 함께 써서 남에게 마음 좁게 행동한다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with 굴다, it means acting narrow-mindedly toward others.

phrases.en: If you say that, you seem narrow-minded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻의 쉬운 말로, 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word with a similar meaning that sounds softer in conversation.

explain_en: Petty and narrow in character, reacting to small matters. It is similar to '속이 좁다', but '옹졸하다' sounds a bit more formal. It is used for a person's mind or attitude. Its opposites are '너그럽다' and '대범하다'.

t90.ax: Don't be petty, just let it go this once.

en: to ridicule; to jeer at; to deride

examples.ko: 손님을 우롱하는 광고에 많은 사람이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Many people were angry at the ad that made fools of customers.

examples.ko: 지금 저를 우롱하시는 거예요?
examples.en: Are you making a fool of me right now?

examples.ko: 그 회사는 소비자를 우롱했다는 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: That company was criticized for toying with consumers.

examples.ko: 우롱하지 마세요. 저도 참을 만큼 참았어요.
examples.en: Don't make a fool of me. I've put up with it long enough.

examples.ko: 고객을 우롱한 직원에게 모두가 실망했어요.
examples.en: Everyone was disappointed in the employee who made a fool of the customer.

examples.ko: 상대를 우롱할 생각은 전혀 없었어요.
examples.en: I had no intention at all of making a fool of the other person.

explain: '놀리다'보다 훨씬 강해서, 상대를 속이거나 바보 취급하며 가지고 노는 느낌이에요. 항의나 뉴스에서 주로 나오고, 일상 말로는 '가지고 놀다'라고 하기도 해요. 당하는 쪽에서는 '우롱당하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The customers felt like they had been made fools of.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우롱을 당하는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person being ridiculed.
phrases.en_equiv: to be made a fool of

phrases.en: Don't say things that make fools of the people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 항의에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in the news and in protests.
phrases.en_equiv: to make a fool of the public

phrases.en: Don't play with people's feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '우롱하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday alternative to 우롱하다.

explain_en: Treating someone as a fool, deceiving or playing with them. It is much stronger than '놀리다', carrying the feel of deceiving someone or treating them like a fool and playing with them. It mostly appears in complaints and the news, and in daily talk people may say '가지고 놀다'. From the victim's side it is '우롱당하다'.

t90.ax: Are you making a fool of me right now?

examples.ko: 의로운 일을 한 사람에게 상을 줬어요.
examples.en: They gave an award to the person who did a righteous deed.

examples.ko: 그는 가난해도 의롭게 살려고 노력했어요.
examples.en: Even though he was poor, he tried to live righteously.

examples.ko: 친구를 위해 나선 모습이 정말 의로워 보였어요.
examples.en: Stepping up for his friend looked truly righteous.

examples.ko: 의롭지 않은 방법으로 이기고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to win by unrighteous means.

examples.ko: 의로웠던 선택 덕분에 많은 사람이 도움을 받았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to that righteous choice, many people got help.

examples.ko: 의롭다고 믿는 일이라면 끝까지 해 보세요.
examples.en: If you believe it's the right thing, see it through to the end.

explain: 옳고 바른 일을 위해 나서는 마음이나 행동을 말해요. '의로운 행동', '의로운 사람'처럼 칭찬하는 글에서 많이 나와요. '정의롭다'와 비슷하지만 '정의'를 더 강조할 때는 '정의롭다'를 써요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '의로워요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: His righteous act was in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옳은 일을 한 행동을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for praising a morally right act.

phrases.en: He is truly a righteous person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성품을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a person's character.

phrases.en: I want to live righteously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 삶의 태도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes one's attitude toward life.

explain_en: It describes a mind or action that stands up for what is right. It appears often in praise, as in '의로운 행동' and '의로운 사람'. It is close to '정의롭다', which puts more weight on justice. It is ㅂ-irregular, becoming '의로워요'.

t90.ax: I don't want to win by unrighteous means.

examples.ko: 그는 의붓자식도 친자식처럼 키웠어요.
examples.en: He raised his stepchild just like his own child.

examples.ko: 의붓자식이라고 차별하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not discriminate against a child for being a stepchild.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 의붓자식 셋을 함께 돌보고 있어요.
examples.en: That couple is raising three stepchildren together.

examples.ko: 의붓자식을 사랑으로 품어 준 분이에요.
examples.en: She is someone who embraced her stepchild with love.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 의붓자식이 주인공으로 나와요.
examples.en: A stepchild appears as the main character in the drama.

examples.ko: 그 아주머니는 의붓자식에게도 늘 따뜻했어요.
examples.en: That woman was always warm to her stepchild as well.

explain: 배우자가 데려온 아이, 즉 재혼한 상대의 자식을 말해요. 아들과 딸을 나누어 '의붓아들', '의붓딸'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: He bought a bike for his stepson.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의붓자식' 중에서 아들만 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers only to the son among stepchildren.

phrases.en: My stepdaughter wrote me a letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의붓자식' 중에서 딸만 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers only to the daughter among stepchildren.

phrases.en: She raised her stepchild with great care.
phrases.nuance_ko: '키우다'와 함께 쓰면 양육하는 모습을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 키우다 to describe raising a stepchild.

explain_en: Stepchild, neutral term. It refers to the child your spouse brings into a marriage, that is, the child of your remarried partner. By gender it can be '의붓아들' (stepson) or '의붓딸' (stepdaughter).

examples.ko: 부모를 버리는 건 인륜에 어긋나는 일이에요.
examples.en: Abandoning one's parents goes against human morality.

examples.ko: 인륜을 저버린 행동에 사람들이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: People were angry at the act that betrayed basic human ethics.

examples.ko: 효는 인륜의 기본이라고 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned that filial piety is the basis of human morality.

examples.ko: 가족을 돌보는 것은 인륜이에요.
examples.en: Caring for family is part of basic human duty.

examples.ko: 법에 없어도 인륜상 해야 할 일이 있어요.
examples.en: Even if the law doesn't say so, there are things we must do as a matter of human duty.

examples.ko: 인륜을 지키며 살고 싶다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: He said he wanted to live upholding human morality.

explain: 사람과 사람 사이, 특히 부모 자식이나 가족 사이에 지켜야 할 도리를 말해요. '인륜에 어긋나다/반하다', '인륜을 저버리다'로 쓰고, 딱딱하고 무거운 말투예요.

phrases.en: It was a crime against human morality, so everyone was outraged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람으로서 지켜야 할 도리를 크게 어긴 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for acts that seriously violate basic human morals.

phrases.en: We should keep to moral duty even within the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람으로서 해야 할 도리를 따른다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means following the moral duties expected of a person.

phrases.en: People who break basic human morals get condemned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도리를 지키지 않았다고 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone for not following moral duty.

explain_en: It refers to the duties people must keep toward one another, especially among parents, children and family. It appears in '인륜에 어긋나다/반하다' and '인륜을 저버리다', in a stiff, serious tone.

en: to be heartless; to be merciless; to be inhumane

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 인정사정없이 공격했어요.
examples.en: The opposing team attacked without mercy.

examples.ko: 인정사정없는 비판에 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: The ruthless criticism hurt my feelings.

examples.ko: 그 상사는 실수에 인정사정없어요.
examples.en: That boss shows no mercy for mistakes.

examples.ko: 추위가 인정사정없이 몰아쳤어요.
examples.en: The cold hit relentlessly.

examples.ko: 인정사정없다고 소문난 감독님이 우리 팀을 맡았어요.
examples.en: A coach known for being merciless took over our team.

examples.ko: 시장 경쟁은 인정사정없어서 방심하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Market competition is ruthless, so you can't let your guard down.

explain: '인정사정없이'처럼 부사형으로 가장 자주 쓰고 붙여서 써요. 사람의 태도뿐 아니라 추위, 경쟁, 공격에도 쓸 수 있어요. '매정하다'는 마음이 차가운 느낌이고, 이 말은 가차 없이 몰아붙이는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: The snowstorm raged without mercy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 가장 자주 쓰고 날씨에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common adverb form, and it can describe weather too.

phrases.en: I survived in a merciless competition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '-는'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -는 when it modifies a noun.

phrases.en: Our team leader is really ruthless about work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝맺는 말로 쓰면 사람의 태도를 직접 평가하는 느낌이 나요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a sentence ending, it sounds like a direct judgment of someone's attitude.

explain_en: Treating people harshly without any leniency; spoken, about training or punishment. It is used most often as the adverb '인정사정없이' and is written without spaces. It applies to cold, competition or attacks as well as people's attitudes. '매정하다' feels coldhearted, while this word stresses pressing on relentlessly.

examples.ko: 저는 컴퓨터는 일자무식이라서 도움이 필요해요.
examples.en: I know absolutely nothing about computers, so I need help.

examples.ko: 요리는 일자무식인데 오늘 처음 김치찌개를 끓여 봤어요.
examples.en: I know nothing about cooking, but today I made kimchi stew for the first time.

examples.ko: 할머니는 일자무식이셨지만 지혜로운 분이셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother couldn't read a word, but she was a wise person.

examples.ko: 그분이 주식에 일자무식이라고요? 의외네요.
examples.en: He knows nothing about stocks? That's surprising.

examples.ko: 글자를 모르는 일자무식에서 시작해 교수가 된 분이에요.
examples.en: He started out unable to read a single letter and became a professor.

examples.ko: 일자무식 소리를 들을까 봐 질문을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was afraid of being called totally ignorant, so I couldn't ask questions.

explain: 글자를 한 자도 모른다는 데서 나와, 글을 모르거나 어떤 분야를 전혀 모를 때 써요. 남에게 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어서 보통 자신을 낮출 때 많이 말해요. 한 분야를 모르는 사람은 '문외한'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I know absolutely nothing about exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분야 + 에는' 뒤에 붙여 자신을 낮추어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to a field plus 에는 to humbly say one knows nothing.

phrases.en: I'm a layperson when it comes to art, so I need an explanation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 분야를 잘 모르는 사람을 점잖게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more polite way to describe someone unfamiliar with a field.

phrases.en: I'm totally clueless about machines, so I can't fix it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하며 문장을 이을 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to give a reason and connect sentences.

explain_en: Colloquial, can sound insulting; person who knows nothing or cannot read. It comes from not knowing even one character, and is used for someone who cannot read or knows nothing about a field. Said about another person it can sound rude, so people mostly use it to put themselves down. A person outside a field can also be called '문외한'.

t90.ax: He knows nothing about stocks? That's surprising.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 나이에 비해 조숙해서 어른처럼 말해요.
examples.en: That child is mature for their age and talks like an adult.

examples.ko: 조숙한 아이들은 또래와 잘 안 맞을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Precocious children sometimes don't fit in with their peers.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 어릴 때부터 생각이 조숙했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has thought like an adult since childhood.

examples.ko: 요즘 아이들은 몸이 일찍 자라서 조숙하다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: Kids these days grow physically early, so people say they mature early.

examples.ko: 조숙하게 자란 탓인지 그는 늘 차분해요.
examples.en: Perhaps because he grew up fast, he is always calm.

examples.ko: 열 살인데도 조숙하니까 대화가 잘 통해요.
examples.en: Although she's only ten, she's mature, so we talk easily.

explain: 나이에 비해 생각이나 몸이 빨리 자랐다는 뜻이라서 칭찬만은 아니에요. 칭찬할 때는 '어른스럽다'나 '의젓하다'를 쓰고, 반대로 아직 덜 자란 느낌은 '미숙하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: She is a precocious child, so she talks like an adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때 쓰는 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form before a noun.

phrases.en: That student looks more mature than his age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 말투가 빨리 자란 것 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone seems to have grown up early.

phrases.example: 제 동생은 조숙하지 않고 아직 아기 같아요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling isn't precocious and is still like a baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 나이에 맞게 자란다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form; grows at a typical pace for their age.

explain_en: It says that mind or body developed early for the age, so it is not purely praise. For praise use '어른스럽다' or '의젓하다', and for the opposite, not yet developed, you say '미숙하다'.

en: to rebuke; to reprimand; to reprove

examples.ko: 기자들은 정부의 늑장 대응을 강하게 질타했어요.
examples.en: Reporters sharply rebuked the government's slow response.

examples.ko: 국회의원들이 장관의 무책임한 답변을 질타하고 있어요.
examples.en: Lawmakers are rebuking the minister's irresponsible answer.

examples.ko: 팬들은 경기 태도를 질타하는 글을 많이 올렸어요.
examples.en: Fans posted many messages criticizing the team's attitude in the game.

examples.ko: 아무리 화가 나도 사람들 앞에서 그렇게 질타하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: No matter how angry you are, you shouldn't scold someone like that in front of people.

examples.ko: 시민들이 불친절한 서비스를 질타해서 회사가 사과했어요.
examples.en: Citizens criticized the unfriendly service, so the company apologized.

examples.ko: 언론은 이번 사고의 책임자를 질타할 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.en: The press had no choice but to rebuke those responsible for the accident.

explain: '비판하다'보다 훨씬 강하고 날카롭게 잘못을 꾸짖는 느낌이에요. 뉴스, 국회, 언론 같은 공적인 자리에서 주로 쓰고, 가족이나 친구 사이에서는 '혼내다'가 자연스러워요. 목적어는 보통 '대응, 태도, 책임자'처럼 잘못한 일이나 사람이에요.

phrases.en: Reporters sharply rebuked the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강하게'를 붙여서 날카로운 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'strongly' emphasizes the sharpness.

phrases.en: Citizens rebuked the government's response.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대응, 태도 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Goes well with words like response or attitude.

phrases.en: Voices of rebuke rose from many places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 비판이 나오는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news for the appearance of criticism.

explain_en: Loud public criticism, by crowds, media or society; written style. It feels much stronger and sharper than '비판하다' (to criticize). It is used mainly in public settings such as the news, the National Assembly and the press, while '혼내다' is more natural among family and friends. The object is usually a wrongdoing or the person responsible, like 대응, 태도 or 책임자.

en: to disdain; to despise; to look down on

examples.ko: 옛날에는 장사하는 사람을 천시하는 분위기가 있었어요.
examples.en: In the past, there was an atmosphere that looked down on merchants.

examples.ko: 어떤 직업도 천시해서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not look down on any occupation.

examples.ko: 그는 노동을 천시하지 않는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is a person who doesn't look down on labor.

examples.ko: 사람을 외모로 천시하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't look down on people because of their appearance.

examples.ko: 신분이 낮다고 천시했던 시대가 있었어요.
examples.en: There was an era when people looked down on others for their low status.

examples.ko: 그들은 장인을 천시했지만 지금은 존경해요.
examples.en: They looked down on craftsmen before, but now they respect them.

explain: '무시하다'보다 신분, 직업, 일 자체를 천하다고 낮게 보는 느낌이 강해서 역사나 사회 이야기에서 잘 나와요. '천대하다'와 가깝고, 반대 느낌의 말은 '존중하다', '중시하다'예요.

phrases.en: In the past, some families treated girls with contempt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '천시하다'와 가깝지만 사람을 낮게 대하는 행동까지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to '천시하다', but also covers treating people badly in action.

phrases.en: Don't look down on any kind of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '천시하다'의 부정 명령형이라 충고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative command form, used when giving advice.

phrases.example: 직업을 천시하는 생각은 이제 많이 사라졌어요.
phrases.en: The idea of looking down on certain jobs has mostly disappeared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '천시하다'가 가장 자주 함께 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical pairing for '천시하다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to look down on a job

explain_en: Treating a job or group as low status (직업) Compared with '무시하다', it stresses seeing a person's status, job or work itself as lowly, so it fits history and social topics. It is close to '천대하다', and its opposites are '존중하다' and '중시하다'.

t90.ax: You must not look down on any occupation.

examples.ko: 그는 바닷가에서 여자 친구에게 청혼했어요.
examples.en: He proposed to his girlfriend at the beach.

examples.ko: 반지를 준비해서 청혼할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll prepare a ring and propose.

examples.ko: 남자 친구가 깜짝 이벤트로 청혼하는 영상을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a video of a boyfriend proposing with a surprise event.

examples.ko: 청혼하기 전에 부모님께 먼저 인사드렸어요.
examples.en: Before proposing, I first paid my respects to her parents.

examples.ko: 청혼해 줘서 정말 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you so much for proposing to me.

examples.ko: 그에게 청혼하고 나서 며칠 동안 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: After proposing to him, I couldn't sleep for several days.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '프러포즈하다'가 더 흔하고, '청혼'은 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. '청혼을 받다/받아들이다/거절하다'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I received a marriage proposal from my boyfriend yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청혼하는 사람이 아니라 청혼을 듣는 사람 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is said from the point of view of the person being proposed to.

phrases.en: She turned down his proposal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청혼을 받아들이지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone does not accept a proposal.

phrases.en: He proposed at a hotel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '청혼하다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk this is more common than 청혼하다.

explain_en: In everyday talk '프러포즈하다' is more common, while '청혼' appears more in writing and the news. The noun is also common: '청혼을 받다/받아들이다/거절하다' (receive/accept/turn down a proposal).
